items.title: The factorization property for Ext one annihilation is preserved by base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an ideal I of a ring R, an object K of D(R) concentrated in degrees -1 and 0, and a ring map R -> R', and asserts that if K satisfies the equivalent conditions of the Ext-one-annihilation statement with respect to (R, I) then tau_{>=-1}(K tensor^L_R R') satisfies the same conditions with respect to (R', IR') (source lines 22552-22561). The proof works with the explicit representing complex. By the equivalent conditions one may assume K is represented by a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 with K^0 free such that for every a in I the multiplication map a : K^{-1} -> K^{-1} equals h_a composed with the differential d_K^{-1}, for some map h_a : K^0 -> K^{-1} (proof lines 22564-22566). The two-term base change statement then shows that tau_{>=-1}(K tensor^L_R R') is represented by K^bullet tensor_R R' (proof lines 22567-22569). The substantive step is the base change of the factorization: for every a in I one has a tensor 1 = (h_a tensor 1) composed with (d_K^{-1} tensor 1), so the required factorization holds after base change (proof lines 22569-22571). Since the collection of maps K^{-1} tensor_R R' -> K^{-1} tensor_R R' factoring through d_K^{-1} tensor 1 forms an R'-module, and IR' is generated by the images of the elements of I, the conclusion follows for the ideal IR' (proof lines 22572-22574). The non-routine content is the observation that the factorization condition is preserved verbatim by base change, together with the module structure that promotes it from the generators of I to the whole ideal IR'.
